papers.title_en: Beyond Infraction Scores: Failure-Boundary Profiles for Closed-Loop Evaluation of Driving and Robot Navigation Agents
papers.authors: Milan Bulat, Gino Ardelean, Ellington Kirby
papers.evidence: 提出失败边界画像用于驾驶智能体闭环评估，并批判违规分数指标
papers.tldr: 闭环驾驶基准用驾驶分数排名智能体，但该分数无法区分“在障碍前停下”和“硬挤过去”这两种失败。为此作者提出失败边界剖面：让每个场景族只改变一个可测因素（如走廊宽度、对向车流时间间隔），并将每个变体认证为应通过或应停止。沿该轴估计每个智能体的承诺概率与胜任概率两条曲线，并用模拟器运行方差给出置信区间，同时得到决策准确率指标。在CARLA七个场景族上评测七个驾驶智能体，规则专家决策准确率为0.74，得分最高的学习智能体TFv6仅0.60；驾驶分数相近的智能体失败方式不同。该方法还直接用于Isaac Sim仓储机器人，发现导航策略仅在三个场景族中的一个能在受阻间隙前停下。
papers.abstract_en: Closed-loop driving benchmarks in CARLA rank agents by a driving score that multiplies route completion by an infraction penalty. This score does not distinguish an agent that stops in front of an obstacle from one that pushes past it. In a corridor closed by two parked cars, for example, one agent that drives through with contact averages 52.2 on the blocked widths, while the agents that stop average between 37.8 and 40.6. We propose failure-boundary profiles, an evaluation in which each scenario family varies one measured factor, such as corridor width or the time gap in oncoming traffic, and each variant is certified from measurement as one where the agent should proceed or one where it should stop. Along this axis we estimate two curves per agent, commitment (the probability of attempting the passage) and competence (the probability of passing without contact), and locate where each crosses one half, with intervals that account for the simulator's run-to-run variance. The certified labels also give a summary metric, decision accuracy, which credits clean passes on passable variants and stops on blocked ones. We evaluate seven driving agents on seven CARLA families. The rule-based expert reaches a decision accuracy of 0.74 and TFv6, the highest-scoring learned agent, 0.60. Agents with similar driving scores fail in different ways, and agents that reliably stop at a blocked corridor still rarely wait for a gap in oncoming traffic. We also apply the method, unchanged, to a warehouse robot in Isaac Sim. The navigation policy we test stops at blocked gaps in only one of three families, and two fine-tuned versions of it pass more gaps cleanly but no longer stop at all.

papers.title_en: Scenario Orchestration for Closed-loop Policy Evaluation of Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Frieda Rong, Zhaoyue Wang, Veer Kapadia, Vishaka Rajani, Aren A. Babikian, Xujie Si, Mahsa Golchoubian, Raquel Urtasun, Igor Gilitschenski
papers.evidence: 面向自动驾驶闭环策略评估的场景编排器
papers.tldr: 闭环仿真中，预编排演员的固定路线和速度会因自车响应而偏离原定交互，脚本化与学习型演员难以可靠复现场景意图。本文提出场景编排器，持续监测联合交通状态，通过重定时、重路由和角色重分配调整非自车演员，并在每步求解受限优化以保持交互、限制干预和维持可行性。CARLA多场景实验表明，该方法比脚本化及学习型基线更可靠地实现目标交互，尤其适应初始条件和自车行为变化。它将场景实现与策略失败分开判断，为可控可复现的自动驾驶闭环评估提供工具。
papers.abstract_en: Scenario-based simulation is central to evaluating autonomous-driving policies, but a scenario scripted before execution (i.e., with predetermined, fixed actor routes and speeds) may not preserve its intended interaction once the tested ego policy responds in closed loop. Scripted scenarios cannot adapt to unanticipated ego behavior, while learned traffic actors may remain reactive without reliably realizing a particular scenario intent. We introduce a scenario orchestrator that continuously monitors the joint traffic state and adapts non-ego actors through re-timing, re-routing, and role reassignment for creating a specific scenario intent. At each step, the orchestrator solves a constrained optimization problem that preserves the intended interaction while limiting interventions and maintaining traffic feasibility. We further distinguish scenario realization from policy failure, allowing a test to first be judged based on whether the intended interaction occurred and then by how the ego policy responded. Experiments in the CARLA simulator across multiple scenario families and driving policies show that orchestration realizes targeted interactions more reliably than scripted and learned actor-level baselines, particularly under variations in initial conditions and ego behavior. These results support closed-loop scenario orchestration as a tool for controlled and reproducible policy evaluation.

papers.title_en: Bug2Scenario: Root-Cause-Preserving Test Scenario Amplification for Autonomous Driving Software
papers.authors: Yuchen Cao, Zhenyu Mao, Jacky Wai Keung, Yifei Wang, Yihan Liao, Jingyu Zhang
papers.evidence: 面向自动驾驶回归测试的根因保持测试场景扩增
papers.tldr: 仿真模糊测试能暴露自动驾驶系统故障，但将单次失败转化为可复用回归场景仍很困难。Bug2Scenario从场景数据、轨迹与判定证据提取根因模式，由LLM提出参与者、任务、路线和天气的语义变体，再用确定性规则生成DriveFuzz兼容场景。在匹配种子和六个LLM骨干下，边界包含保持率提升10.6个百分点（p=0.011），严格保持率提升6.7个百分点但不显著；反馈可帮助部分初始失败种子产出严格保持候选，种子级停止减少额外调用。该框架为ADS回归测试提供根因保持的场景放大资产。
papers.abstract_en: Simulation-based fuzzing exposes autonomous driving system (ADS) failures by repeatedly mutating and executing scenarios, but converting one failure into reusable regression scenarios remains difficult. Such variants test whether the mechanism persists after software changes, for example by varying weather or actor placement while retaining a collision's actor-route conflict. We present Bug2Scenario, a root-cause-guided post-fuzzing framework. From scenario data, traces, and oracle evidence, it extracts a root-cause pattern. An LLM proposes semantic variations over actors, missions, routes, and weather. Deterministic rules construct DriveFuzz-compatible scenarios. Execution evidence and manual review assess preservation. Separating these responsibilities prevents fluency, syntax, or recurring labels from masquerading as causal evidence. Under matched seeds, six LLM backbones, candidate budget, and execution pipeline, Bug2Scenario improves strict preservation by 6.7 percentage points (p=0.104; not significant) and boundary-inclusive preservation by 10.6 points (p=0.011). Feedback helps some initially unsuccessful seeds yield a strictly preserved candidate. Seed-level stopping then avoids further API calls and simulator runs. Remaining failures reflect actor-placement constraints, simulator instability, and incomplete or conflicting causal evidence. Bug2Scenario thus produces reliable ADS regression assets. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/YgcCoder/Bug2Sce.

papers.title_en: Attack Injection to Vehicle Reactions: Extensible Closed-Loop Adversarial Evaluation Framework
papers.authors: Mohamed Gaber, Tahsin Wahid, Mohammad Mamun, Salimur Choudhury
papers.evidence: 面向自动驾驶系统的可扩展闭环对抗评估框架
papers.tldr: 车路协同信息被伪造时，自动驾驶应用可能作出不安全决策，需追踪消息到车辆反应与交通交互的闭环影响。作者基于VaN3Twin构建可扩展闭环对抗评估框架，集成76个攻击配置、9类攻击套件和带标签数据集，连接实时注入、网络传输、接收应用与车辆运动反馈。实验确认全部攻击配置可执行，各套件均产生与受攻击消息关联的请求，并观察到受攻击车辆经未篡改消息间接影响他车。该框架支持直接与间接交通效应研究，且可扩展攻击、消息路径、应用和日志字段。
papers.abstract_en: Autonomous vehicles can use information exchanged with other vehicles and roadside infrastructure to support driving decisions. However, applications that rely on this information can make unsafe decisions when it is falsified. Studying the resulting traffic effects requires following received information through application decisions, vehicle reactions, and subsequent interactions. We present an extensible closed-loop adversarial evaluation framework built on VaN3Twin, a platform for traffic and wireless network simulation, with a diverse attack library and a labelled dataset covering benign and attack conditions. A key advantage of the framework is that it can be extended with additional attacks, message paths, receiving applications, and logging fields. The added library contains 76 configurable attack profiles adapted to message formats defined by the European Telecommunications Standards Institute. These profiles are organized into nine groups of related attacks, referred to as suites. The framework connects live attack injection and simulated network delivery to receiving applications, whose selected commands update vehicle movement. The resulting state feeds subsequent message generation, closing the loop. The dataset links physical vehicle states and message exchanges to attack labels, application decisions, selected commands, and traffic outcomes. Evaluation with individual and combined attack suites confirmed execution of all profiles, and every suite produced requests linked to attacked messages. A recorded sequence also showed a vehicle reacting to an attacked message and subsequently influencing another vehicle through an unmodified message describing its updated movement. These findings demonstrate how live injection and vehicle feedback support the study of direct and indirect effects as traffic evolves.

papers.title_en: URL-Sim: Unified and Regulated LiDAR Simulation for High-Fidelity Reconstruction of Dynamic Driving Scenes
papers.authors: Kefei Qian, Xipeng Feng, Jie Li, Long Cao, Yuhan Chen, Xiangfei Huang, Guofa Li
papers.evidence: 用于自动驾驶安全验证的高保真激光雷达仿真
papers.tldr: 从真实驾驶日志重建高保真 LiDAR 仿真场景，对自动驾驶安全验证至关重要。现有基于 NeRF 的仿真器渲染慢，基于 3DGS 的方法又局限于刚性车辆且图元冗余。URL-Sim 提出统一的动态高斯场景图，解耦建模车辆、行人与骑行者，并用受调控的致密化策略按多维重要性分配高斯。在 Waymo 和 KITTI-360 上，同等图元预算下精度与视觉质量优于基线，并能准确恢复多样动态参与者的几何与位姿。
papers.abstract_en: Reconstructing high-fidelity LiDAR simulation scenes from real-world driving logs is essential for cost-effective safety validation of autonomous driving systems. While simulators based on Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) achieve realistic scene reconstruction, their large-scale adoption is limited by slow rendering speeds. Recent 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) approaches have improved rendering efficiency through explicit primitive representation and differentiable rasterization. However, existing 3DGS-based methods remain largely restricted to rigid vehicles and produce redundant primitives through unconstrained densification. To address these limitations, we propose URL-Sim, a unified and regulated dynamic LiDAR simulation framework. URL-Sim constructs a dynamic Gaussian scene graph that decouples the modeling of traffic participants, including vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists, enabling accurate reconstruction of heterogeneous dynamic objects within a single framework. It further introduces a regulated Gaussian densification strategy that ranks primitives with multi-dimensional importance scores and allocates Gaussians to the most critical regions while keeping the total primitive count bounded. Experiments on the Waymo and KITTI-360 datasets demonstrate that URL-Sim achieves higher quantitative accuracy and visual quality than existing baselines under comparable primitive budgets, and accurately recovers the geometry and poses of diverse dynamic traffic participants.

papers.title_en: CoSafe: Cooperative Runtime Safety Assurance for Mixed-Traffic Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Dingji Wang, You Lu, Haowen Jiang, Yanggang Chen, Yuyang Bi, Bihuan Chen, Shenglin Bao, Xin Peng
papers.evidence: 面向自动驾驶系统的运行时安全保障与风险监控
papers.tldr: 混合交通中自动驾驶仍频发安全违规，现有以自车为中心的接管难以处理多车局部合理但联合冲突的决策。CoSafe利用V2X让路侧单元监测场景级风险，并对涉及多车的危险进行协同干预。在InterDrive上集成七种先进ADS，驾驶分数平均提升70.03%，安全违规减少87.80%，识别不安全AV的F3达0.930且满足实时约束。该框架把运行时保障从单车接管扩展到场景级协同干预。
papers.abstract_en: With the rapid development of autonomous driving systems (ADSes), real-world roads are evolving into mixed-traffic environments where autonomous vehicles (AVs) and other traffic participants (e.g., human-driven vehicles (HDVs), cyclists, and pedestrians) coexist and interact with each other. However, current ADSes still incur various safety violations in mixed traffic scenarios, raising a strong demand for runtime safety assurance frameworks that can continuously monitor hazards and prevent potential violations. Existing ego-centric assurance approaches are insufficient for mixed traffic, where violations often arise from locally reasonable yet jointly incompatible decisions among multiple vehicles and cannot be reliably resolved through independent takeover.   To bridge this gap, we propose CoSafe, a modular and ADS-agnostic cooperative runtime safety assurance framework for mixed-traffic autonomous driving to extend runtime safety assurance from ego-centric takeover to scene-level cooperative intervention. CoSafe leverages vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication to enable roadside units (RSUs) to monitor scene-level hazards and jointly mitigate hazards involving multiple vehicles. We integrate CoSafe with seven state-of-the-art ADSes, and our evaluation on the InterDrive benchmark demonstrates that CoSafe improves the driving score of AVs by 70.03% on average, reduces safety violations by 87.80%, and accurately identifies unsafe AVs with an F3 score of 0.930, while satisfying real-time constraints.

papers.title_en: Training-Independent Validation of a Learning-Based Controller for Stunt Maneuvers
papers.authors: Kiruthiga Chandra Shekar, Aliasghar Arab, Jingang Yi
papers.evidence: 基于Sim2Real2Sim回路的训练无关验证
papers.tldr: 学习型车辆特技控制器常在训练条件内验证，看似可靠，却未覆盖真实道路中变化的物理参数。本文提出独立于训练的验证思路：改变训练固定的物理参数，并采用训练目标之外的验收标准。针对G-Maneuver（报告成功率90.11%），较宽松的终端航向评分甚至把最差设置排为最佳；再以Sim2Real2Sim循环筛选真车安全区，真车接受率16.9%。结果表明航向变化、侧滑和速度归一化横摆率可跨仿真与实车匹配，而力与侧倾指标不匹配，为安全部署筛选可用指标。
papers.abstract_en: Learned controllers for vehicle maneuvers are usually validated under the conditions and objective used to train them, where they appear highly reliable, yet the parameters that change on real roads are often not those the model was trained on. We argue that validation must be independent of training: it should vary physical parameters that training kept fixed and use acceptance criteria absent from the training objective. A learning-based control policy, G-Maneuver, with 90.11% success is tested for stunt-level maneuvers. A looser terminal-heading score ranked the worst setting as the best. Because real stunt tests are safety-critical, a simulation-to-reality-to-simulation (Sim2Real2Sim) loop uses the simulation to select safe zones for real-vehicle trials with 16.9% acceptance. Automotive safety analysis frameworks are used to identify parameters for validation using coverage tests. We demonstrated that the kinematic stunt-driving indicators, namely heading change, sideslip, and speed-normalized yaw rate, match between simulation and the real world, while force and roll indicators do not, which identifies the indicators that can support safe deployment. A video of the experiments is available at https://youtu.be/dN1Oes8pNIo.

papers.title_en: WAM-Sim0.1: World Anchored Memory Meets Online RL for Consistent and Realistic Driving Simulation
papers.authors: Jiahao Cui, Jiaye Li, Wenhao Zhang, Yaoyi Li, Shan Luan, Quanhui Tang, Jianhua Han, Lin Cheng, Hang Xu, Siyu Zhu
papers.evidence: 驾驶世界模型生成一致且真实的仿真，用于自动驾驶测试
papers.tldr: 自回归驾驶世界模型因条件信号瞬时、缺乏持久状态，长时推演易出现结构漂移、身份漂移与质量衰减。WAM-Sim以层次化持久记忆锚定道路拓扑、背景外观和交通参与者身份，并用在线flow-matching强化学习优化自生成rollout。在nuScenes上取得FID=3.47、FVD=25.72及24.16 mAP、71.23 road mIoU。分钟级推演显著缓解漂移，提升场景一致性与身份连贯性。
papers.abstract_en: Autoregressive driving world models systematically suffer from structural drift, identity drift, and quality decay over long rollout horizons due to transient conditioning signals that lack persistent state. We present WAM-Sim, a driving world model anchored by a persistent hierarchical memory and optimized via online flow-matching RL. WAM-Sim structures persistent context across three temporal and semantic scales: pose-aligned structural tokens encoding persistent road topology, read-only scene tokens supplying geolocated background appearance, and write-once instance tokens preserving individual traffic participant identities across occlusions and chunk boundaries. To restore visual sharpness and physical plausibility degraded by multi-scale conditioning, we introduce an online post-training framework that optimizes self-generated rollouts via flow-matching RL guided by hierarchy-aligned visual rewards and a vision-language model physical judge. The invariant memory empirically confines policy optimization within the anchored context, helping suppress semantic collapse and reward hacking, while online RL systematically enforces physical commonsense and fine-grained visual fidelity. On the nuScenes benchmark, WAM-Sim achieves a superior generation fidelity (FID=3.47, FVD=25.72) and strong downstream perception performance (24.16 mAP, 71.23 road mIoU). On minute-scale rollouts of self-collected data, WAM-Sim substantially mitigates structural and identity drift, preserving high scene similarity and subject identity coherence across extended horizons. Project page: https://fudan-generative-vision.github.io/WAM-Sim.

papers.title_en: Genie Sim Benchmark: Real-to-Sim Fidelity and Evaluation
papers.authors: Di Yang, Da Huang, Yang Lv, Fan Yang, Yi Lu, Zheyuan Xing, Linting Guo, Jiaen Shen, Wenjun Sun, Maoqing Yao, Qian Wang
papers.evidence: 针对仿真基准的真实到仿真保真度评估与仿真-真机一致性度量
papers.tldr: 针对机器人仿真评测中真实-仿真一致性难以量化的问题，Genie Sim Benchmark 通过22组真实-仿真配对任务与系统辨识实验进行评估。方法上结合任务专用 pi0.5 策略、长时闭环位置/关节力矩对比、对象辨识与跨引擎接触迁移，并另用32.6503秒遥操作轨迹检验外部位置目标。结果显示任务得分相关系数0.9686、MAE 0.0405，关节位置RMSE 0.00614-0.03522 rad，力矩RMSE 0.73545-4.00099 N·m。该基准支持同时考察任务结果与物理响应一致性。
papers.abstract_en: We evaluate Genie Sim Benchmark through paired real-simulation tasks and complementary system-identification studies. Across 22 robot-task pairs spanning 16 task names, task-specific pi0.5 policies fine-tuned on real-robot data achieve a descriptive Score correlation of 0.9686, MAE 0.0405, RMSE 0.0520, with simulation-real differences from -0.110 to +0.080. G2 crsB experiments assess long-horizon closed-loop position and joint-side torque agreement, while five representative object cases examine identification and cross-engine contact transfer. A separate 32.6503 s teleoperation trajectory, excluded from mechanical identification and servo-gain search, evaluates external position targets through simulated motion-controller command shaping and a calibrated position servo. Across both arms, per-joint position RMSE spans 0.00614-0.03522 rad and current-derived torque RMSE spans 0.73545-4.00099 N m. Native PhysX adaptations recover three recorded interaction tasks, with case-dependent alignment gains. These results support task-specific simulation evaluation through joint assessment of task outcomes and physical-response consistency.

papers.title_en: Interactive World Simulation with Cosmos for Physical AI
papers.authors: NVIDIA, :, Anis Ahmad, Jon Allen, Malik Aqeel Anwar, Jesse Archer, Maciej Bala, Piotr Barejko, Aarti Basant, Dan Blick, Taras Bolzhelarskyi, Henry Che, Jin Chen, Yukang Chen, Tae Eun Choe, Yuzhu Dong, Nat Duca, Liang Feng, Francesco Ferroni, Xiao Fu, Mohit Gambhir, Vivek Goel, Rony Goldenthal, Aryaman Gupta, Ali Hassani, Nathan Hayes-Roth, Yong He, Michael Honke, Shengyu Huang, Wei Huang, DeLesley Hutchins, Suneel Indupuru, Pooya Jannaty, Jingyi Jin, Janmesh Kalra, Ashna Khetan, Xin Kong, Aleksandr Korovko, Hui Kuang, Zhengfei Kuang, George Kurian, Jean-Francois Lafleche, Jayjun Lee, Justin Leung, William Lew, Xiang Li, Zhaoshuo Li, Chen-Hsuan Lin, Ming-Yu Liu, Xiangyu Lu, Yuhang Lu, Martin Ding Ma, Qianli Ma, Aditya Mahajan, Miguel Martin, Janarbek Matai, Jonathan McCaffrey, Qing Miao, Ashkan Mirzaei, Mustafa Munir, Sangmin Oh, David Pankratz, Trung Pham, Marilyn Reeb, Gavriel State, Jiaxiang Tang, Shitao Tang, Yue Tang, Tolou Tavakkoli, Alexander Temirov, Hweimi Tsou, Sergei Vasilev, Thomas Volk, Andrew Z. Wang, Hao Wang, Shijie Wang, Zhonghao Wang, David Wehr, Shumian Xin, Mengyao Xu, Yao Xu, Shuai Yang, Sophia Zalewski, Pengcuo Zeren, Cindy Zha, Jing Zhang, Yuliya Zhautouskaya, Kaiwen Zheng, Andrew Zhu, Rick Zhuang
papers.evidence: 用于训练与评估的自动驾驶仿真环境
papers.tldr: Physical AI训练与评估需要可实时交互的虚拟环境，现有世界模拟难以统一响应动作与场景控制。本文提出基于Cosmos世界基础模型的共享框架，以流式视觉观察回应用户与具身智能体的动作，并支持从外部模拟器物理状态生成观测。框架在相机导航、机器人操作、可控视频迁移和多视角自动驾驶仿真中演示。它为构建Physical AI交互式虚拟环境提供共享基础，并开源代码与模型检查点。
papers.abstract_en: We present a shared framework that adapts Cosmos world foundation models for real-time interactive world simulation in Physical AI. By streaming visual observations in response to actions and scene controls, the framework enables users and embodied agents to interact with evolving virtual environments. It supports both predicting the visual consequences of actions and generating observations from physical state maintained by an external simulator. We demonstrate this approach across camera navigation and robot manipulation, controllable video transfer, and multi-view autonomous vehicle (AV) simulation. These examples provide a shared foundation for developing interactive virtual environments for Physical AI training and evaluation. Our code and model checkpoints are available at https://github.com/nvidia/cosmos and https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/cosmos3-examples. The project website is available at https://research.nvidia.com/labs/cosmos-lab/cosmos-simulation.

papers.title_en: EGT: Execution-Grounded Traversability through Learned Closed-Loop Trajectory Distributions
papers.authors: Chinmay Mundane, Amith Manoharan, Arun Kumar Singh
papers.evidence: 用于路径执行评估的闭环轨迹分布度量
papers.tldr: 崎岖地形可通行性常用逐点姿态或力角裕度估计，但忽略地形扰动与底层控制器修正，易失真且保守。本文提出执行落地可通行性EGT，定义为车辆-控制器对执行候选路径并满足轨迹跟踪与前进要求的概率，用潜空间流匹配预测闭环轨迹分布，并融合多分辨率地形、3D姿态与轮地接触先验。仿真650次未见地形试验中，安全路径误拒降至2.2%，危险路径误收7.7%；嵌入滚动时域采样规划器后，导航失败率显著下降，并实现仿真训练模型到户外实车的零样本迁移。
papers.abstract_en: Rough terrain traversability is often estimated through point-wise roll, pitch, or force-angle margins along a planned path. However, these metrics are often inaccurate and overly conservative because they ignore how terrain disturbances and low-level controller corrections can affect the vehicle's motions. To overcome these limitations, we introduce Execution-Grounded Traversability (EGT), defined as the probability that a vehicle-controller pair can execute a candidate path while meeting trajectory-level tracking and progress requirements. We estimate EGT by predicting the distribution of closed-loop trajectories using a latent-space flow matching (FM) model conditioned on multi-resolution terrain features and 3D vehicle attitude and wheel-ground contact points prior. Across 650 simulated trials on unseen terrains, EGT reduces safe-path rejection to 2.2% (versus 11.4%-39.5% for pose-margin and force-angle baselines) and unsafe acceptance to 7.7%. Integrated into a receding-horizon sampling-based planner, EGT reduces navigation failure rates by 24-42 and 30-44 percentage points over [1] and [2], respectively, while cutting goal-reaching time by up to 20.5% and 45%. Finally, we demonstrate zero-shot transfer of our simulation-trained model to real-world outdoor experiments.

papers.title_en: CrossLiDAR: Controllable Multi-Sensor LiDAR Sequence Generation
papers.authors: Khanh Nguyen, Thomas Walker, Hichem Telli, Carlos de la Torre-Ortiz, Stefano Fiorini, Salah Eddine Bekhouche, Mohammed-En-Nadhir Zighem, Wassim Swaileh, Tinghuai Wang
papers.evidence: 面向自主系统可扩展开发与验证的高保真激光雷达仿真
papers.tldr: 激光雷达仿真生成对自动驾驶系统的可扩展开发与验证至关重要，但现有生成器通常只支持单一传感器配置、对结构与几何的控制有限，且长时4D生成易漂移。CrossLiDAR提出统一的Transformer框架，在距离图紧凑潜空间中使用rectified flow目标与MM-DiT骨干，结合跨传感器交互模块和ControlNet式结构条件分支，实现可控且时空一致的多传感器激光雷达序列生成。模型以短N帧序列自回归扩展以增强长时连贯性，在nuScenes和Waymo上JSD平均提升29.56%、MMD提升15.36%，显著优于现有基线。该工作通过长时程、标定一致的多传感器rollout，为可控的场景化自动驾驶测试仿真提供了新途径。
papers.abstract_en: High-fidelity LiDAR simulation remains a bottleneck for scalable development and validation of autonomous systems. Existing generators can synthesize realistic scans, but they are typically constrained to a single sensor configuration, offer limited control over structure and geometry, and drift in long-horizon 4D generation. We present CrossLiDAR, a unified transformer-based framework capable of generating controllable and spatio-temporally consistent multi-sensor LiDAR sequences. Our approach leverages a rectified flow objective with a Multi-Modal Diffusion Transformer (MM-DiT) backbone, within a compact latent space of range images. To support multiple LiDAR sensors, an Inter-sensor Module enables interaction across sensors, while a ControlNet-style branch provides structural conditioning (e.g., BEV priors or 3D bounding boxes). For modeling the temporal consistency, CrossLiDAR generates short $N$-frame sequences and extends them autoregressively to improve long-horizon coherence. Our model significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving an average improvement of 29.56\% in JSD and 15.36\% in MMD evaluated on nuScenes and the Waymo Dataset. CrossLiDAR bridges the gap to modern autonomous-driving simulation by enabling calibration-consistent multi-sensor LiDAR rollouts over long horizons for controllable, scenario-based testing.

papers.title_en: DriveFoundry: Co-Evolving Data and Model for Efficient Closed-Loop Iteration in Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Ziyang Yao, Yuncheng Jiang, Fang Li, Haochen Liu, Shaoqing Xu, Wen Zhang, Xiangyang Chu, Zibin Guo, Jiale Hou, Chuang Wan, Jia Hua, Gengzhao Xiang, Xiaoran Luo, Chong He, Yuechen Luo, Junzhe Wang, Zhiyu Sun, Jun Zhang, Wei Li, Lei Li, Hongwei Xie, Bing Wang, Yuannan Shen, Jianwei Cui, Guang Chen, Hangjun Ye, Jingwei Zhao
papers.evidence: 带结果评估的自动驾驶模型闭环迭代框架
papers.tldr: 自动驾驶基础模型需从稀有事件学习可复用决策，并在严格运行时约束下应用。DriveFoundry耦合因果数据精炼与自适应推理，用可追踪场景-候选记录和模型失败驱动标注修正。Xiaomi-Drive-o1在共享视觉语言骨干中统一感知、因果、动作、世界与价值，并动态分配计算。9B模型在PhysicalAI取得最低ADE@1，AlpaSim多项指标优于Alpamayo 1.5；0.8B联合训练使5秒minADE@6降约54%，自适应推理仅用28% token，支持高效闭环迭代。
papers.abstract_en: A driving foundation model must learn reusable decision knowledge from rare critical events and apply it under strict runtime constraints. We introduce DriveFoundry, a closed-loop framework improving iteration efficiency under data and computation budgets by coupling structured causal data refinement with adaptive inference. The Data Engine builds traceable scene-candidate records linking scene evidence and factor-decision relations to candidate trajectories and outcome assessments. Candidate comparisons and counterfactual annotations clarify how scene factors affect behavioral feasibility and preference. Verified model failures guide VLM-assisted annotation and expert correction, refining training data and annotation systems. The model engine, Xiaomi-Drive-o1, unifies Perception, Causation, Action, World, and Value within a shared vision-language backbone to enable cross-task knowledge transfer. Block-wise latent refill passes candidate-specific evidence and predicted visual consequences between task blocks, connecting scene understanding, planning, and evaluation. A learned value-of-computation head selects tasks and allocates latent tokens based on expected benefit and cost, adapting inference to each decision. On PhysicalAI, the 9B model achieves the lowest ADE@1 across evaluated splits and horizons among tested models. In AlpaSim, it outperforms Alpamayo 1.5 across all metrics and achieves lower close-encounter and off-road rates than the 34B Alpamayo 2 Super, while trailing in progress and AlpaSim scores. For the 0.8B variant, joint training reduces 5 s minADE@6 by about 54% without altering the inference path or token budget. Adaptive inference matches full reasoning performance using only 28% of tokens. Real-vehicle tests confirm runtime feasibility, supporting a unified paradigm for learning from critical experience and dynamically allocating computation.

papers.title_en: RiSE-Drive: Risk-Sensitive Long-Horizon Candidate Evaluation for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Yu Zhao, Hongyi Duan, Ming Yin, Hongyuan Zhang, Fan Yang, Hongzhi Wang, Xiubo Liang
papers.evidence: 端到端驾驶中风险敏感的长时程候选评估框架
papers.tldr: 端到端自动驾驶通常先生成多条候选轨迹再打分选择，但现有评估多用确定性点分数或单结果评价，难以刻画长时程延迟失效、尾部风险与排序不稳定。RiSE-Drive 先做候选条件化的潜在未来推演，估计长时程结果分布，再用尾部风险感知且抗扰动的准则对候选排序。在 NAVSIM-v1、NAVSIM-v2 与闭环 HUGSIM 上取得 SOTA，并显著提升候选选择的鲁棒性。
papers.abstract_en: End-to-end autonomous driving systems increasingly rely on generating multiple trajectory candidates and selecting one for execution. In this setting, a central challenge is no longer only candidate generation, but how to evaluate candidates according to their long-horizon consequences under uncertainty. Existing methods still mainly use deterministic point scores, heuristic subscores, or single-outcome evaluations, which makes it difficult to capture delayed failures, tail risk, and ranking instability under plausible future perturbations. We present RiSE-Drive, a framework for risk-sensitive long-horizon candidate evaluation in end-to-end autonomous driving. RiSE-Drive first performs candidate-conditioned latent future rollout, then estimates long-horizon outcome distributions instead of single scalar scores, and finally ranks candidates using a tail-risk-aware and perturbation-robust decision criterion. This reformulates candidate scoring from deterministic oracle-style evaluation into distributional outcome assessment with explicit risk control. As a result, the evaluator is encouraged to prefer candidates that are not only strong under nominal conditions, but also reliable under long-horizon rollout and safety-critical deviations. Experiments on the NAVSIM-v1 and NAVSIM-v2 benchmarks, as well as the closed-loop HUGSIM benchmark, show that RiSE-Drive achieves state-of-the-art performance and significantly improves the robustness of candidate selection.

papers.title_en: BirdDreams: Joint Perspective and BEV Video Generation for a Plausible, Reactive Driving World Model
papers.authors: Junyoung Seo, Jaewoo Seo, Seungryong Kim, Laura Leal-Taixé, Xiuming Zhang, Seung Wook Kim
papers.evidence: 可反应的驾驶世界模型在自车动作下模拟可信场景演化，用于测试
papers.tldr: 驾驶世界模型需同时模拟自车轨迹可控与周围车辆合理运动，但仅从透视视频学习运动易受外观耦合和遮挡影响。BirdDreams自回归联合生成透视视频与示意BEV视频，并用双流扩散Transformer的联合注意力互相补充。BEV作为几何接口实现自车轨迹软条件，推理仅需单张相机图像。在PhysicalAI-AV和nuScenes上更忠实跟随自车轨迹，并生成更合理的自车与周围车辆行为。
papers.abstract_en: Driving world models aim to simulate how a scene unfolds under different ego actions. This requires plausible motion of surrounding vehicles as well as precise ego-trajectory control. Learning vehicle motion from perspective video alone is challenging because motion is entangled with appearance and vehicles can be occluded. Prior work therefore conditions video generation on layouts that specify vehicle motion, providing control over surrounding vehicles but requiring their future trajectories as inputs. We introduce BirdDreams, an autoregressive driving world model that jointly generates perspective video and a schematic bird's-eye-view (BEV) video, making scene layout part of the predicted future. The BEV, rendered from scene annotations for training, depicts roads and vehicles as simple shapes at a fixed metric scale, providing a top-down view of their positions and motion with reduced occlusion between vehicles. Perspective video, by contrast, retains scene details that the BEV omits, such as traffic signals and object appearance. Joint attention between two video diffusion transformers, one per stream, lets each stream inform the other during generation. The predicted BEV also provides a geometric interface for ego control: we translate and rotate its latest frame along an input ego trajectory and use the resulting frames as a soft condition that shows how the scene would appear to move if only the ego vehicle moved. At inference, BirdDreams generates both videos from a single camera image without requiring an HD map or vehicle-state inputs. On PhysicalAI-AV and nuScenes, BirdDreams follows input ego trajectories more faithfully than prior driving world models and generates more plausible ego motion without ego-action conditioning. Human evaluation shows that BirdDreams outperforms a perspective-only baseline in generating realistic surrounding-vehicle behavior.

papers.title_en: Evaluating Video LLMs' Understanding of Corner Cases in Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Gabriel Manalu, Minh Son Hoang, Hyeontaek Hwang, Jaesung Lee, Hyojin Choi, Tran Tuan Phong, Seon Kwon Kim, Saad Wazir, Daeyoung Kim
papers.evidence: 面向极端场景的驾驶模型评测基准
papers.tldr: 现有驾驶场景基准多聚焦常规交通与通用理解，难以评估Video LLMs在罕见且安全关键的corner cases上的表现。作者提出DashBench，用1,709段精心筛选的驾驶视频测试25个Video LLMs，覆盖碰撞与非碰撞罕见事件，并通过丰富提示与开放式问答评测。结果显示所有模型均远低于安全关键应用阈值，常误判或漏检前方危险事件，并在解释中幻觉不存在的交通参与者或动作。该工作以数据集、评测工具和局限诊断推动更安全可解释的自动驾驶系统。
papers.abstract_en: Natural language explanations promised by modern Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) offer autonomous driving systems a path toward detailed scene description and interpretable decision making on the road. While recent benchmarks have begun assessing these models on driving scenes, they mainly target routine traffic conditions and general comprehension tasks based on existing driving datasets and therefore fail to evaluate model performance on the rarest and most safety-critical driving events, also known as "corner cases". To provide a comprehensive evaluation of Video LLMs on precisely these scenarios, we introduce DashBench, a benchmark testing 25 Video LLMs on 1,709 carefully curated driving videos spanning not only collision-related corner cases but also rare non-collision ones. Through extensive prompts and open-ended question answering, we expose a critical capability gap: all evaluated models perform substantially below the threshold required for safety-critical driving applications, frequently misjudging or missing dangerous events on the road ahead and hallucinating non-existent agents or actions in their explanations. We believe DashBench, combining an extensive dataset with a rigorous evaluation toolkit and a detailed diagnosis of current model limitations, drives progress toward safer, more explainable autonomous driving systems. The code and data will be shared at: cornercase-dashbench.github.io
